item.title: Tiger Woods to return to competitive golf next month
item.description: Tiger Woods will return to competitive golf for the first time in more than two years next month when he tees off at the Hero World Challenge event in the Bahamas, organisers said on Tuesday. Woods, 50, was named in the line-up for the limited field PGA Tour event taking place in Albany from December 3-6. It will mark the first time Woods has played an official PGA Tour event since July 2024. The 15-time major champion has battled injuries and legal problems since his last appearance. In March he was involved in a rollover car crash in Florida which led to him having his driver’s license suspended for five years. Authorities determined the 15-time major champion had not been drinking alcohol but found he appeared to be impaired. Woods, who has undergone multiple back operations and surgeries on severe leg injuries suffered in a separate 2021 California car crash, had two pills containing the opioid painkiller hydrocodone in his pocket. He refused a urine analysis and was charged, jailed and released on bond. Woods initially pleaded not guilty to charges of DUI (driving under the influence) with property damage and refusing to submit to a lawful test. Days later, he said he was “stepping away” to seek treatment and focus on his health. Since the crash, Woods has travelled outside the United States to seek treatment at an inpatient facility, reportedly in Switzerland. He made his first public appearance since his arrest at the PGA Tour’s Travelers Championship in June, and later struck a plea agreement which led to his driver’s license being suspended. Woods has not won a tournament since a victory at the ZoZo Championship in Japan in 2019. The post Tiger Woods to return to competitive golf next month appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: INEC warns against attacks on staff, threatens sanctions
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has warned against any form of harassment, intimidation or physical attack on its leadership, staff members or ad hoc workers by political supporters. INEC ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‍‌‌‌⁠‍⁠‌​Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, gave the warning on Tuesday in Abuja at the 2026 Goodluck Jonathan Foundation (GJF) Peace and Security Conference. Amupitan, represented by INEC National Commissioner, Mrs May Agbamuche-Mbu, described election officials as public servants discharging a sacred constitutional duty. He warned that assaulting or threatening them constitutes a direct assault on the Nigerian state and would be met with decisive legal consequences. Amupiatan also condemned the widespread incidents of political violence, intimidation and attacks on campaign convoys and party supporters recorded in some parts of the country in recent weeks. According to him, democracy can not flourish in an atmosphere of fear and bloodshed. “Let me issue a clear and unambiguous warning to all political actors, sponsors and their foot soldiers: “The law will take its full course and security agencies working alongside the commission will go after the promoters and perpetrators of violent campaigns without fear or favour. “Equally, I must sound a stern warning against any form of harassment, intimidation or physical attack directed at the leadership, staff or ad hoc workers of INEC by supporters of any political party—whether within Nigeria or abroad. “Election officials are public servants discharging a sacred constitutional duty; assaulting or threatening them is an assault on the Nigerian state and will be met with decisive legal consequences,’’ he said. Amupitan reminded political parties and candidates of the provisions of the Electoral Act 2026, noting that sections 96 and 97 prohibit abusive language, private thugs and use of force to intimidate voters. He said that the Act raised financial penalties five-fold, imposing fines of up to five million Naira or 12 months imprisonment on individuals and up to 10 million Naira on political parties for initial breaches. The INEC chairman added that under Section 148, INEC was statutorily empowered to prosecute electoral offenders directly upon receiving case files from the police. On physical security and logistics, Amupitan said that the commission was leveraging the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES) to secure the electoral terrain against insurgency, banditry and communal tensions. To tackle digital misinformation on elections, he said that INEC had established a dedicated Artificial Intelligence Division within its ICT Department. He said that the department was established to monitor database anomalies, verify digital assets and counter deepfakes, synthetic broadcasts and Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference (FIMI). item.title: Abia records 60% drop in maternal mortality — Govt
item.description: …Renovates 190 PHCs, functionalises 123, Polytechnic rector emerges Administrator of the Year By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Abia State Government has announced a 60 per cent reduction in maternal mortality between 2024 and 2026, claiming that the state now has the second-lowest maternal mortality rate in the country. The government attributed the improvement to ongoing reforms in the health sector, including the rehabilitation of primary healthcare facilities and increased investment in healthcare delivery. Commissioner for Information, Prince Okey Kanu, disclosed this during a briefing on the outcome of this week’s State Executive Council meeting at Government House, Umuahia. He was represented by the Special Adviser to the Governor on Media and Publicity, Mr Ferdinand Ekeoma. Kanu said the administration had made significant progress in its efforts to revitalise primary healthcare, disclosing that 190 of the 200 primary healthcare centres earmarked for renovation under Project Ekwueme had been completed. Of the renovated facilities, 123 had been functionalised to provide essential medical services, while 27 had been equipped with solar power, with work progressing on nine additional centres. He also announced the completion of all 77 World Bank-supported health projects in the state. In another development, the Commissioner disclosed that the Aba Campus of the College of Nursing Sciences had secured an increase in its admission quota from 75 to 120 students following an accreditation exercise by the National Nursing and Midwifery Council. The new quota, according to him, was communicated in an accreditation report released on November 13 and reflected growing confidence in the state’s investment in nursing education and healthcare manpower development. Meanwhile, the Rector of Ogbonnaya Onu Polytechnic, Aba, Dr Christopher Okoro, has emerged Administrator of the Year in a nationwide poll organised by Leadership Excellence Award. Kanu said Okoro secured 148,267 votes in the exercise, which recognised his contributions to institutional transformation, human capital development and technical and professional education. He attributed the recognition to developments recorded at the institution under the Rector, including a student population increase of more than 6,000, improved infrastructure and better staff welfare. The Commissioner also said the state government remained committed to education development, noting that the sector continued to receive 20 per cent of the state’s annual budget. On public health surveillance, the government reported that Abia recorded no cases of Ebola, Lassa fever, COVID-19, diphtheria, cholera, mpox or yellow fever during the period under review. The Commissioner for Health, Prof. Enoch Ogbonnaya Uche, who also addressed the briefing, provided an update on the Ebola situation in the country. item.title: Kano woman allegedly hires men to kill co-wife’s children for inheritance
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Kano State Police Command has arrested a 20-year-old woman and three others over an alleged plot to kill her husband’s four children from another wife to enable her only son to inherit his father’s properties. The suspects were arrested following the abduction and killing of a 14-year-old boy, identified as Mahmoud Auwal, who was allegedly targeted as part of the plan. The Police Public Relations Officer, CSP Abdullahi Haruna Kiyawa, disclosed this on Tuesday. According to the police, the victim’s mother reported his abduction on April 29, 2026, at Danbare Quarters in Kumbotso Local Government Area of Kano State. Following the report, the Commissioner of Police, Ibrahim Adamu Bakori, directed operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Squad to investigate the incident. The command said its operatives arrested the first suspect, Muhammad Musa Isma’il, 20, of Sharada Quarters, Kano, on November 3, 2026. “During interrogation, he confessed to luring the victim on April 20, 2026, and identified Abubakar Muhammad Isah, 27, and Auwal Muhammad, 26, as his accomplices,” Kiyawa said. The police said the suspects allegedly conspired to kill the teenager and abandoned his body at the scene. His remains were later recovered by police officers attached to Kwalli Division while on patrol and taken to the mortuary of Sir Muhammad Sunusi Specialist Hospital. Further investigations led to the arrest of Hajiya Rukayya Auwal, 20, of Mararaba Quarters, New Karu Local Government Area of Nasarawa State, whom the police identified as the alleged mastermind. The command said the suspects claimed that they carried out the crime on her instructions. It added that investigations revealed that Rukayya was the deceased’s father’s other wife and allegedly wanted to eliminate all four children of her co-wife so that her only son would inherit their father’s properties. “The principal suspect also allegedly engaged another group of thugs to attack Muhammad Musa Isma’il in Mararaba, Karu Local Government Area of Nasarawa State, in a bid to stop him from revealing the crime,” the police said. The command said the suspects would be charged to court after the conclusion of investigations. The Commissioner of Police condemned the killing and assured the victim’s family and members of the public that the command would ensure justice was served. He also called on residents to continue providing credible information to the police to assist in preventing and detecting crime. item.title: Two die, Gombe APC chairman, campaign DG injured in crash
item.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe The Gombe State Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Mohammed Dantata Ndus, and the Director-General of the party’s 2027 Governorship Campaign Council, Sa’du Hassan, have sustained injuries in a road accident that claimed two lives in Dasan Yunusa community. The accident occurred on Tuesday along the Deba-Talasse Junction while the two party officials were travelling to join the campaign entourage of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya in Balanga North Local Government Area of the state. The APC State Campaign Council confirmed the incident in a statement, identifying the deceased as Haruna and Kabiru, both indigenes of Dasan Yunusa. It said the two APC chieftains sustained injuries and were receiving medical attention at the Federal Teaching Hospital, Gombe. Preliminary accounts indicated that the accident occurred when the driver conveying the party officials reportedly swerved to avoid a head-on collision with a motorcycle carrying three persons, which allegedly appeared suddenly at the junction. The vehicle reportedly veered off the road in the process, resulting in the fatal incident. Confirming the accident, the Gombe State Sector Commander of the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), Samson Kaura, said he had received information about the incident but was awaiting comprehensive details. Kaura confirmed that the APC chairman and the campaign council’s Director-General were receiving treatment, adding that further information would be provided as investigations progressed. The campaign council expressed sorrow over the incident and extended its condolences to the bereaved families, the people of Dasan Yunusa and others affected by the tragedy. Meanwhile, Governor Yahaya, who was leading the APC campaign activities in the area, visited Dasan Yunusa following news of the accident to commiserate with the bereaved families and community leaders. The governor described the incident as painful and unfortunate, noting that the loss of two lives had cast a shadow over what was intended to be a day of political engagement with the people. He urged the bereaved families and residents to accept the tragedy as the will of Almighty Allah. Yahaya prayed for the repose of the souls of the deceased in Aljannatul Firdaus and for strength for their families to bear the loss. As part of efforts to support those affected, the governor donated N5 million to the families of the deceased and the community leadership. He also prayed for the speedy recovery of those injured, particularly Ndus and Hassan, who were reported to be stable and responding to medical care. The governor’s visit and donation followed the fatal accident that disrupted the party’s campaign activities in the area. The post Two die, Gombe APC chairman, campaign DG injured in crash appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: New Nasarawa police chief warns against extortion
item.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia The new Commissioner of Police in Nasarawa State, Sheikh Mohammed Danko, has warned officers and personnel against intimidation, extortion, unlawful detention and abuse of police authority. Danko, who has assumed duty as the 32nd commissioner of police in the state, said the police uniform represented a responsibility to serve the public and not a licence to operate above the law. He replaces Muhammed Shettima Jauro, who has been elevated to the rank of Assistant Inspector-General of Police. Addressing journalists at the command headquarters in Lafia, Danko said his administration would not tolerate corruption, excessive use of force, harassment or any misuse of police authority. He said: “Any officer found engaging in misconduct, political partisanship, corruption, or abuse of power will face immediate and appropriate disciplinary and legal actions.” The commissioner said complaints against police personnel would be treated seriously and thoroughly reviewed through the appropriate channels. He added that officers found culpable would be held accountable, irrespective of their positions, while personnel who discharged their duties honourably would receive the command’s support. Danko also cautioned political actors against using their offices or influence to intimidate citizens, provoke violence, obstruct lawful police duties or shield individuals from accountability. He directed officers to remain professional and non-partisan, warning against political pressure and private interests that could compromise their responsibilities. On security, the commissioner warned criminal elements involved in kidnapping, armed robbery, drug trafficking, cult-related activities and other violent crimes that the command would respond through intelligence-led and lawful operations. He also warned individuals providing shelter, weapons, information or other support to criminal networks that they could face the full weight of the law. Danko called for greater cooperation between the police and residents, urging community leaders, traditional institutions, youth groups and business owners to report suspicious activities through appropriate channels. He said public cooperation was essential to effective policing and reaffirmed the command’s commitment to protecting residents, enforcing the law impartially and strengthening public confidence across the state. The commissioner also advised residents against taking the law into their own hands or confronting suspects, warning that such actions could endanger lives and jeopardise investigations. The post New Nasarawa police chief warns against extortion appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ebonyi demolishes shop over planning violations
item.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The Ebonyi State Government has demolished a shop on Ejiofor Street, Abakaliki, over alleged failure to obtain building plan approval and encroachment on designated land. The demolition was carried out by the Ministry of Capital City and Urban Planning. Speaking during the exercise, the Commissioner for Capital City and Urban Planning, Richard Ugo Idike, said the property owner commenced construction without obtaining the required building plan approval from the ministry. Idike explained that building plan approval was mandatory to enable the ministry assess proposed structures, conduct necessary inspections and provide professional guidance to ensure compliance with physical planning standards. He said securing approval before commencing construction would also allow the ministry to identify potential structural, environmental and planning concerns and advise property owners accordingly. The commissioner cautioned property owners and developers against unauthorised construction and encroachment on designated lands, warning that the state government would enforce relevant planning regulations against defaulters. Idike was accompanied during the exercise by the Head of the Town Planning Department, TPL Esther Nwite, other town planners and members of the ministry’s task force. He urged residents, developers and property owners in Abakaliki to obtain the necessary building plan approval from the ministry before embarking on construction projects. The commissioner reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to enforcing physical planning regulations and promoting orderly development in the state capital. The post Ebonyi demolishes shop over planning violations appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.description: …the only permanent thing in life is change – group leader By Peter Duru, Makurdi In a significant political development ahead of the 2027 Benue state governorship election, seven former commissioners who served under Governor Hyacinth Alia have declared their support for the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate, Chief Michael Aondoakaa, SAN, pledging to work towards his emergence as the next governor of the state. They described the former Attorney-General of the Federation as a leader with the requisite exposure and administrative experience to provide purposeful leadership and reposition the state for sustainable development. “The group pledged its commitment to mobilising support for Aondoakaa’s governorship ambition and expressed optimism about his ability to address critical issues affecting the state,” the statement said. Others were Joyce Luga, former Commissioner for Cooperative, Urban and Rural Development; Mr Omale Omale, former Commissioner for Power, Transport and Renewable Energy; and Matthew Aboh, former Commissioner for Information, Culture and Tourism. item.title: Tinubu transmits mental health amendment bill to Senate
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has transmitted the National Mental Health Amendment Bill, 2026 to the Senate, seeking decriminalisation of attempted suicide and support for survivors. Senate ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‍‌​‌‌‍​‌​President Godswill Akpabio, who announced the transmission during plenary on Tuesday, said that the proposed amendment would address concerns surrounding criminal penalties for attempted suicide. Akpabio said his earlier comments had excluded persons experiencing mental illness, whose condition could affect their ability to understand their actions when attempting suicide. “Perhaps, with this amendment, I should make a distinction in my earlier submission. “I had said that if someone attempts suicide, such a person should ensure that the attempt succeeds. Otherwise, the person would be sent to prison. “However, I did not include people who are mentally disturbed. I made that distinction because they do not have the mental balance to understand what they are doing. “I want to thank the president for supporting the decriminalisation of attempted suicide because making it a criminal offence for people who are mentally disturbed would be insensitive,” he said. Akpabio said the amendment was important, adding that the bill would decriminalise attempted suicide, particularly in cases involving people who were mentally disturbed. “When I made my earlier submission, I clearly stated that I was referring to people who were mentally sound, not those who were mentally disturbed. Unfortunately, social media reports did not capture that distinction. “Nevertheless, this is a welcome development. People who are mentally disturbed require our support,” he added. The senate president, thereafter, referred the bill to the Committee on Rules and Business for further legislative action, urging its consideration as soon as practicable. item.title: Elumelu raises Seplat stake to 22.05%
item.description: By Ozumba Chika Tony Elumelu, Chairman of Heirs Holdings, has increased his stake in Seplat Energy Plc to 22.05 per cent following the acquisition of additional shares valued at approximately $70 million. The latest purchase, made through Heirs Energies Limited, involved 5,888,341 ordinary shares, representing about one per cent of the company. The transaction was disclosed to the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX) on Tuesday in a notification signed by Edith Onwuchekwa, Seplat Energy’s Director, Legal and Company Secretary. According to the disclosure, Heirs Energies Limited, a company controlled by Elumelu, acquired the shares from the company. Following the transaction, Heirs Energies’ direct shareholding in Seplat rose to 33,832,208 shares. The disclosure added that entities controlled by Elumelu — Heirs Energies Limited and Heirs Holdings Limited — now hold a combined 132,288,341 shares, representing a voting interest of 22.05 per cent of Seplat’s issued share capital of 599,944,561 shares. The company said the notification was made in compliance with Rule 17.15(c) of the NGX Rulebook 2015 on disclosure of dealings in issuers’ shares and Article 19(3) of the United Kingdom Market Abuse Regulations. The latest acquisition follows a similar transaction in September, when Elumelu, through Heirs Energies, purchased six million Seplat shares for £53.2 million. That transaction raised the combined shareholding of Heirs Energies and Heirs Holdings in the company to 21.07 per cent. Meanwhile, Seplat also disclosed a separate insider transaction involving its Chairman, Udoma Udo Udoma. The company said Tierce Investments Limited, a firm wholly owned by Udoma, purchased Seplat Energy’s 9.125 per cent Senior Unsecured Notes due March 21, 2030. The notes had a face value of $370,000, while the cash consideration for the purchase was $397,076.81. The post Elumelu raises Seplat stake to 22.05% appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Passenger vows never to fly United Nigeria Airlines over early departure – Okonkwo
item.description: By Dickson Omobola Executive Chairman of United Nigeria Airlines, Professor Obiora Okonkwo, has said a passenger sent him a message last week threatening never to fly with the airline again because it departed earlier than its advertised time. Okonkwo said the passenger complained that while United Nigeria Airlines advertised an 11:30am departure, it took off at 11:20am. He spoke during a dialogue on Responsible Business Communication: Building Trust and Financing Investments for Sustainable Human Development at the 2026 World Public Relations Forum, WPRF, in Abuja, where he urged organisations to always tell the truth, saying it was the best reputation management strategy. He said: “A typical Nigerian traveller has his mind set on the timely departure of the airline, and if anything happens, you have to communicate the truth. You may have an AOG, technical issues, and sometimes that message doesn’t really sink. “I had a passenger last week who sent me a message saying they will never fly United Nigeria Airlines anymore and I said, why? He said, because they left on time. He said United Nigeria Airlines advertised departure for 11:30am but departed at 11:20am, and as the chairman, I was actually worried about how to respond. “I wanted to get angry, I wanted to shout back at him. But again, my experience being a member of this forum came into play, and I simply sent him a message saying, ‘I apologise for United Nigeria Airline leaving on time.’ That was my answer. He never got back.” He also recounted an incident in which UNA diverted to Asaba instead of Abuja, saying the aircraft was scheduled to fly from Lagos to Abuja but landed in Asaba following an error by the dispatcher, who mistakenly entered Asaba as the destination in the flight documentation. He said the pilots followed the destination indicated in the documents and landed accordingly, while the cabin crew, believing they had arrived in Abuja, welcomed passengers to the Federal Capital Territory. According to him, the incident itself was not necessarily a major crisis until the airline’s communication team issued an inaccurate explanation. Okonkwo said the airline’s communication team, in an attempt to protect the company’s reputation, attributed the incident to bad weather in Abuja, despite the fact that the aircraft had landed in Asaba because of an error in its flight documentation. He, however, maintained that organisations must not confuse reputation protection with withholding or manipulating facts, warning that attempts to conceal the truth could eventually cause greater damage than the original crisis. He added that telling verified truths demonstrates respect for stakeholders and helps build confidence in an organisation, irrespective of how uncomfortable the information might be. He said: “The best word of public relations is to tell the truth and challenge responsibly. item.title: 2027: Kalu promises Tinubu 75% votes in South-East
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Chief Benjamin Kalu, has assured President Bola Tinubu that the South-East will deliver 75 per cent of its votes to him in the January 16, 2027 presidential election, insisting that the President should not have to negotiate for 25 per cent support in the zone. Kalu gave the assurance during the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Abia State, where he said party members were mobilising voters across communities to secure Tinubu’s re-election. He said the APC was going from house to house and village to village to canvass support for the President, adding that the party was determined to demonstrate its electoral strength in the state. According to him, Tinubu has attracted several infrastructural interventions and political appointments to the South-East and would do more if re-elected. Kalu said: “Mr President, the numbers you have in Abia will give you the votes you are looking for. Nobody should convert you to a beggar of 25 per cent. “We have about 12.3 million voters in Abia State. We have millions of members of APC. We have told ourselves that each person will bring 10 people, 10 voters to vote for you. And that will give us 1,620,000 and more votes for you. “That is about 75 per cent of the votes registered voters in Abia State. Mr President, let nobody deceive you that he is working to get 25 per cent for you in Abia.” The Deputy Speaker also disclosed that supporters had assembled 100 branded vehicles for distribution across the state as part of the campaign mobilisation. He said the January 16 election would provide an opportunity for the people of Abia to demonstrate their appreciation for Tinubu’s interventions. Kalu dismissed suggestions that the APC lacked a significant presence in Abia, pointing to the turnout at the rally as evidence of the party’s support base. “We are not sleeping. We are going from house to house. We are going from village to village. We are going from community to community. We are not playing our politics in Abuja,” he said. The APC governorship candidate in Abia State, Chief Eric Opah, also expressed confidence in the party’s growing support base, assuring that its members were committed to Tinubu’s re-election. Similarly, party stakeholders from the three senatorial districts — Chief Emeka Stanley of Abia South, Hon. Cosmas Ndukwe of Abia North and Chief Henry Ikoh of Abia Central — pledged their support for the President, citing his administration’s interventions in the South-East. The Managing Director of the South-East Development Commission (SEDC), Chief Mark Okoye, said Tinubu had demonstrated commitment to the development of the region through the establishment of the commission. Earlier, the Abia APC Chairman and state coordinator of the presidential campaign, Hon. Chijioke Chukwu, declared that the state was an APC stronghold and pledged that it would deliver 90 per cent of its votes to Tinubu.

item.title: Reps to probe 22 states over unpaid pensions
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has resolved to investigate reports that 22 states are failing to pay retirement benefits regularly, amid concerns over the hardship facing thousands of pensioners across the country. The resolution followed the adoption of a motion of urgent public importance sponsored by Rep. Adesola Adebayo, representing Apapa Federal Constituency of Lagos State, at plenary on Tuesday. Moving the motion, Adebayo cited a report indicating that only 14 of Nigeria’s 36 states pay pensions regularly, while the remaining 22 owe retirees several months or, in some cases, years of outstanding entitlements. He described pensions as an earned right rather than a privilege or charity, arguing that public servants who had devoted between 30 and 35 years to service deserved to receive their retirement benefits without unnecessary hardship. The lawmaker expressed concern that many pensioners aged between 70 and 90 were struggling to afford food, medication, rent and other basic necessities, with some reportedly dying in poverty. He also criticised prolonged verification exercises that require elderly retirees to queue for hours or days under harsh weather conditions, citing reports of pensioners collapsing and dying during such exercises. Adebayo argued that the failure to pay pensions undermined constitutional provisions and human dignity, while creating anxiety among serving public workers about their prospects after retirement. The motion, however, generated debate among lawmakers over the constitutional powers of the National Assembly to intervene in pension matters involving state governments. Opposing the motion, Rep. Mark Essiet argued that pension obligations of state governments fell within the jurisdiction of state authorities and their respective Houses of Assembly. He cautioned against any proposal for the Federal Government to deduct funds from states’ allocations to settle outstanding pension liabilities, describing such a move as unconstitutional. Rep. Umoh urged the House to focus on the pension challenges facing military personnel, who, he said, had repeatedly protested over their entitlements. Similarly, Rep. Dominic Okafor cautioned against generalising the allegations against all states, noting that some governors had fulfilled their pension obligations. He cited Anambra State as an example, arguing that the motion should distinguish between states with outstanding pension liabilities and those meeting their responsibilities. However, Rep. Billy Owasaro urged lawmakers not to abandon the motion but to amend provisions that might fall outside the constitutional powers of the National Assembly. He said the plight of elderly pensioners was too serious to be ignored. “We know what our fathers are going through. item.title: Reps move to protect Nigerians displaced by Gabon demolition
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has called for urgent intervention to protect thousands of Nigerians, particularly Ilaje fishermen, reportedly displaced after authorities in Gabon demolished their homes and business premises. The resolution followed the adoption of a motion of urgent public importance moved by Rep. Donald Ojogo at plenary on Tuesday. Presenting the motion, Ojogo expressed concern over the fate of thousands of Nigerians who were reportedly displaced last week following the demolition of their residences along Gabon’s fishing coast. He said the affected Nigerians, predominantly of Ilaje extraction, had lived and conducted fishing and related businesses in Gabon for decades. The lawmaker warned that the demolition had left many of them homeless and exposed to health risks and other humanitarian challenges. He said the situation required urgent diplomatic intervention by the Nigerian Government to prevent further hardship and ensure that the rights and welfare of the affected citizens were protected. Ojogo maintained that the government had a responsibility to safeguard Nigerians wherever they resided, including those living and working outside the country. He cited Section 14(2)(b) of the 1999 Constitution, which identifies the security and welfare of the people as the primary purpose of government, as well as the provisions of Chapter II on the Fundamental Objectives and Directive Principles of State Policy. The lawmaker also drew attention to regional protocols governing the Gulf of Guinea, particularly provisions relating to the protection of marine resources and fishing activities. The House unanimously adopted the motion through a voice vote, urging the Federal Government to establish the circumstances surrounding the demolition and take necessary steps to protect the welfare and rights of the affected Nigerians. It subsequently mandated its Committees on Foreign Affairs, Diaspora, Inland Waterways, and Cooperation and Integration in Africa to urgently intervene and investigate the circumstances surrounding the displacement. The committees are also expected to ascertain the welfare and living conditions of the affected Nigerians, particularly the Ilaje fishermen, and submit their findings to the House within 14 legislative days. item.title: 2027: Anambra set for Tinubu campaign rally
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu AWKA — Anambra State is preparing to host a mega campaign rally in support of President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, with members of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) and the All Progressives Congress (APC) expected to participate. The rally, tagged “SoluTinubu 2027”, is scheduled to hold on Thursday, November 19, 2026, at Dr Alex Ekwueme Square, Awka. According to the state’s Presidential Campaign Council, the event is expected to attract party members from the 326 political wards across Anambra State and demonstrate the level of support for Tinubu’s re-election campaign. The organisers said the rally was anchored on the mantra of “progressives working together”, a political message being promoted by Governor Chukwuma Soludo. Preparations for the event are already underway, with Dr Alex Ekwueme Square and its surroundings undergoing decoration ahead of the rally. The event is also expected to attract prominent political figures from across the South-East and other parts of the country, as supporters are expected to use the gathering to publicly declare their backing for Tinubu ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election. item.title: Army Arrests Seven Suspects, Recovers 38 Phones, Mercedes-Benz In Plateau
item.description: Troops of Sector 1, Joint Task Force, Operation Enduring Peace, have arrested seven suspected criminals and recovered 38 mobile phones, a Mercedes-Benz E350, a motorcycle and other items in separate operations in Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State. The spokesperson for the Joint Task Force, Captain Chinonso Oteh, disclosed this while presenting the suspects at the task force headquarters in Jos, where he gave details of the operations. According to the task force, the arrests followed intelligence-led operations conducted on November 6 and 10, 2026, as part of efforts to curb armed robbery, phone snatching and other criminal activities in the state. In the first operation, troops acted on a report of a phone-snatching incident involving a gunman. The report led to the identification of the location of the stolen phone at Prime House Hotel, along Ring Road, Jos North. A raid on the hotel resulted in the arrest of five suspects. Items recovered during the operation included 26 mobile phones, 27 phone pouches, three MP3 devices, two earpods, an HP laptop, a dagger, four power banks and a Mercedes-Benz E350 with registration number Plateau BBK-01NB. The task force said a further search of the suspects’ vehicle, after it was towed to the Sector 1 headquarters, led to the recovery of 12 additional mobile phones, bringing the total number of phones recovered in the operation to 38. In a separate operation on November 10, troops deployed at Naraguta, working with members of the Vigilante Group of Nigeria, arrested two more suspects during a routine patrol. The suspects were reportedly found with a suspected stolen Boxer motorcycle and a toy pistol. The task force said the seven suspects and the recovered items would be handed over to the Plateau State Police Command for further investigation and possible prosecution. The Commander of Operation Enduring Peace, Major General Maxwell Dangana, reaffirmed the task force’s commitment to combating crime and sustaining peace across its joint operations area. He said the task force would continue to rely on intelligence-driven operations and collaboration with other security agencies and local vigilante groups to tackle criminal activities. Dangana also urged residents to remain vigilant and provide credible and timely information to security agencies to support efforts to restore and sustain lasting peace in Plateau State. item.title: Tinubu Approves Establishment Of Kebbi Inland Dry Port
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has approved the establishment of an inland dry port in Kebbi State as part of efforts to boost economic activities and improve trade in the state. The President announced the approval on Tuesday during the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Birnin Kebbi, the state capital. He also pledged to approve additional road infrastructure projects for the state following requests by Governor Nasir Idris. The rally, held at the Birnin Kebbi Stadium, attracted thousands of APC supporters who gathered to express their support for Tinubu’s re-election bid ahead of the 2027 presidential election. Vice President Kashim Shettima and other party leaders were also present at the event, which featured speeches and goodwill messages from party chieftains. ﻿ Speaking at the rally, Governor Idris expressed satisfaction with the turnout and pledged that Kebbi State would deliver 100 per cent of its votes to Tinubu in the 2027 election. Also addressing the crowd, the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulazeez Yari, said the President had done much for the North-West, including Kebbi State. Yari attributed the large turnout to Tinubu’s acceptance in the region, citing the Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway project, which he said would pass through more than 200 kilometres of Kebbi State. In his remarks, Shettima urged residents of the North to support Tinubu’s re-election, recalling the President’s support for the late President Muhammadu Buhari, who governed Nigeria for eight years. He said Tinubu had stood by Buhari during his political journey and throughout his administration. Taking the podium, Tinubu thanked the people of Kebbi for their support and commended Governor Idris for his leadership. He subsequently announced the approval of some federal projects requested by the governor, including the establishment of the Kebbi Inland Dry Port. The rally also featured goodwill messages from the Speaker of the House of Representatives, the Deputy President of the Senate and other APC leaders and supporters. item.title: Radda Warns Against ‘419 Politicians’ As Supporters Rally For APC In Katsina
item.description: Katsina State Governor, Malam Dikko Umaru Radda, has urged voters to reject what he described as “419 politicians” in the 2027 general elections, declaring that only leaders with proven records of service deserve the people’s mandate. The governor appealed on Tuesday during the Tinubu/Dikko 2027 Campaign Council rally at the Mai’adua International Border Market in Mai’adua Local Government Area, where thousands of APC supporters gathered as the campaign tour continued across the Daura Senatorial Zone. Addressing the enthusiastic crowd, Governor Radda said the massive turnout reflected public confidence in his administration’s performance, particularly in healthcare delivery, education, teacher recruitment, youth empowerment and other development programmes. Supporters rally for Tinubu in Katsina State. He expressed appreciation to the people of Mai’adua for their overwhelming support and pledged to consolidate on the achievements of his administration if re-elected. “We have nothing to say but to thank God for the people of Mai’adua. We are grateful for the support we have received from women, youths and the elderly. This massive turnout shows that the people are satisfied with our achievements and leadership, especially in healthcare, education, teacher recruitment and empowerment.» “Please don’t make the mistake of electing 419 politicians. I know you are not in support of such politicians, and by the grace of God, we will reciprocate this confidence if re-elected. You have also demonstrated that you are genuine supporters and true admirers of the late President Muhammadu Buhari.” The governor also welcomed thousands of defectors from the African Democratic Congress (ADC) into the All Progressives Congress (APC), describing the development as further evidence of the ruling party’s growing popularity across the state. The rally’s highlight was the presentation of an Award of Excellence to Governor Radda by health workers in Mai’adua Local Government Area in recognition of what they described as his transformative leadership and commitment to strengthening the state’s healthcare sector. Earlier, Governor Radda commissioned the newly constructed Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) Dumurkul Division in Mai’adua Local Government Area. The security facility was built by the Chairman of Mai’adua Local Government, Hon. Mamman Salisu Na-Allahu, as part of efforts to strengthen grassroots security and enhance the fight against insecurity in the border communities. Commissioning the project, Governor Radda commended the council chairman for his foresight and commitment to safeguarding lives and property, stressing that security remains the cornerstone of his administration’s development agenda. He charged officers of the NSCDC to uphold professionalism, diligence, and discipline in the discharge of their duties while fostering stronger collaboration with other security agencies and host communities.
